Subject: Planned failover window + driver rollback contingency — Nov 18 (US-West)

Hi Joel / Acme ops team,

Wanted to give a heads-up about a planned maintenance window that will affect the US-West serving pool where your workloads are pinned. This is a targeted failover and driver compatibility sweep intended to address a kernel-driver mismatch we've seen at high load. Key details below: 

- Window: Wednesday, Nov 18, 2026 — 01:00 — 03:00 PT (two-hour runway)
- Impact: We expect transparent failover for most requests; a small fraction (~0.5%) may observe transient 5xxs or increased latency during node evictions.
- Mitigation: automatic route diversion to warm spares, rolling restarts in small batches, and an immediate rollback plan to the currently pinned driver if we see increased error rate.
- Action for customers: No action required unless you rely on long-lived pinned connections; if so, please reply with any concerns and we can discuss a targeted plan.

We've attached the runbook and a short impact matrix for Acme. Marcus will be on shift and will execute the rollout; Monica will coordinate customer notifications and post-window follow-up. Sean will manage the rollback playbook and SLA tweaks if needed.

Attachments: maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB), impact-matrix-acme.csv (CSV)

Runbook link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/infra/maintenance/runbooks/2026-11-18-maintenance-runbook
Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-11-18-us-west-maintenance

Thanks — appreciate your patience. We'll post live updates to the status page during the window.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor

Thanks Grace — appreciate the notice. A couple quick questions from our side: 

1) We run a small batch job that keeps a persistent HTTP/2 connection to US-West endpoints for streaming results; should we expect that to drop and reconnect gracefully?
2) Is there any chance this touches our dedicated tenancy pool (we have a Dedicated reservation with you)?

If there's a recommended change on our side (short-term backoff or connection refresh), let me know and we'll implement it. Otherwise the window looks doable.

—Joel

Quick tech notes to loop in here so Acme has visibility: 

- Persistent HTTP/2 streams: we will drain connections gently; streams are expected to reconnect. For long-lived streams we will enable an aggressive keepalive probe and allow reconnection backoff of up to 45s. If Acme needs a larger grace period, we can schedule their subset in the last batch.
- Dedicated tenancy: your account is on a reserved Dedicated pool, not impacted by the general tenant rotation. We will not evict Dedicated reservations unless explicit opt-in. Acme is safe in that sense.
- Rollback trigger: error rate > 2.5% sustained for 3 minutes OR CPU scheduling anomalies on more than 10% of restarted nodes. If triggered, Sean will kick rollback and we will notify via status and direct email.

I'll be on the runbook console (SSH jump to maintenance-control). Sean — please prep the driver rollback command sequence and confirm the smoke test payload. Monica — please send an updated note to Joel summarizing that dedicated pools are excluded.

—Marcus

- We'll still run a small canary at 01:00 PT to validate driver handshakes; that canary will be limited to 2 nodes and will not affect production traffic.
- If everything looks healthy by 01:20 PT we'll proceed in 10-minute micro-batches. If we see any regression we will trigger rollback (JIRA-INC-4721) and switch primary routing to our warm spares.

I'll post a minute-by-minute update to the status page and also ping your team in the status channel. Attached is the final two-page customer note and the Acme-specific impact matrix.
